newsitem.title: CHINA: China-born children join families enter Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: China-born children join families enter Hong Kong.

text.p: Dozens of children who were born in China, some of them stranded there for years without their families, walked across the border on Friday to join their parents in Hong Kong.

The youngsters streamed through the border gates shortly after they opened near the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, armed with the new one-way permits granting them residence in the wealthy territory.
Some 60 children waved the permits with excitement as they walked through a counter set aside for their customs' clearance.
Hong Kong reverted from British rule on July 1 and is now a Special Administrative Region of China.
Friday's group was the first batch of children to obtain the controversial "certificates of entitlement", documents that they must have before they can live in Hong Kong legally.
Some 66,000 children in China are waiting to join their families in Hong Kong, and the administration has said the new system would allow them to come in the next few years.
Hundreds and possibly thousands of children have been smuggled into Hong Kong in past years to dodge the long immigration queues on the mainland.
But pro-democracy groups and law experts have condemned the new "certificates" system as a contravention of the Basic Law, Hong Kong's mini-constitution which took effect on July 1.
The law granted the children automatic residency rights by virtue of their having at least one parent resident in Hong Kong.

However, Hong Kong's new China-appointed Provisional Legislative Council (PLC), which replaced an elected colonial legislature just after the handover, passed a law in July requiring the certificates before the children can enter Hong Kong.
The law also threatens to deport young Chinese immigrants who had sneaked illegally into Hong Kong in the past.
Hong Kong's new administration has defended the hastily enacted law, passed in just one day, as necessary to stop a flood of immigrants who would weigh down stretched resources.
But a member of the popular Democratic Party criticised the new system on Friday as a blatant violation of the Basic Law.
"It is proven that the children have already the right to come in. (But) now they can come in only when the one-way visa is issued," said Law Chi-kwong on government-funded radio.
The new system could see difficult days ahead.

Many children threatened with deportation have lined up to fight the new immigration law in court, a move that could spark a constitutional crisis as they are questioning the legality of the PLC itself.
A China-backed Hong Kong newspaper on Friday welcomed the new batch of immigrants to Hong Kong, but sounded an ominous warning.

"As for all those Chinese immigrants who have sneaked into Hong Kong illegally, they definitely cannot be given any leeway. Without lawful verification, they cannot become Hong Kong permanent residents," the Ta Kung Po said in an editorial.
